sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Grid-Tie Solar Inverters and Microinverters

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code) with unitary national corporate law; no separate state-level incorporation regime
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1985) and Income Tax Treaty (1984/2018 Protocol)
France–United States Tax Convention (1994, as amended)
EU Free Trade Agreements (e.g., with Canada (CETA), Japan (EPA), South Korea (FTA))
Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (OECD/CoE), as amended by the 2010 Protocol
Eurasia? Note: France has ~60 additional active BITs, including with Algeria, Morocco, India, Singapore and Vietnam.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF) Articles L561-1 to L561-48; French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles L. 561-45 and L. 561-46 (beneficial owner register); Decree No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 (UBO filing and registration procedure); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD) as transposed; Declerq & TRACFIN guidance on risk-based AML/CFT;
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_note: The French UBO register (RCS, maintained by INF/INPI) is not fully public. Access is available to competent authorities (TRACFIN, tax authorities, law enforcement) and to private parties who demonstrate a legitimate interest (e.g., financial institutions, journalists, NGOs) under strict conditions. It is not a fully-open public registry.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Registration (Kbis or equivalent) of any foreign corporate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial/company registry of the parent company's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin country is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise full consular legalization at the French embassy/consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Existence Certificate) issued within the current calendar year
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Companies in the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of legal representatives' and UBOs' passports
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of each representative/UBO; subsequent notarial authentication in the country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and legal representative (utility bill or bank statement or certificate of residence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company, banking institution, or municipal authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (original or notarized true copy)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each UBO and signatory (confirming banking history and no adverse AML findings)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or account-holding bank of the shareholder/UBO

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for pre-incorporation formalities (if a third-party agent will sign the articles)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against (i) TRACFIN/AMF published PEP and national sanction lists; (ii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions (restrictive measures under CFSP); (iii) UN Security Council sanctions; (iv) OFAC/SDN list for USD-denominated correspondences and Swift payments; (v) French national asset-freezing orders (Arrêtés de gel des avoirs). For a low-risk standard industrial scope (ISIC 2790), a simplified due diligence tier applies, but the corporate filing must still screen all UBOs and signatories against these lists before incorporation and maintain records for five years under CMF L561-20.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) for incorporation filings; name availability and prior-rights search via Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr) and INPI's trademark/company-name database (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may include non-French script only if accompanied by a legitimate transliteration/transcription into Latin script. Mandatory French-language filings under the Loi Toubon require that any document binding an employee or public filing uses French; the legal form suffix 'SAS' or 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' must appear on all Company Kbis extracts and statutory filings. The proposed name must be sufficiently distinctive and must not infringe prior trademarks or existing RCS registrations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque (bank) – requires prior authorization from the ACPR
État / République / Préfecture / Ministère (state/republic/prefecture/ministry) – requires ministerial authorization
Chambre de Commerce (chamber of commerce) – reserved for official chambers
Commune / Département / Mairie (municipality/department/town hall) – requires relevant public entity approval
Notaire / Avocat / Pharmacien / Médecin (notary/lawyer/pharmacist/doctor) – subject to specific professional regulations
Bourse / Marché réglementé (stock exchange / regulated market) – reserved for licensed financial market operators
National / Européen / Mondial (national/european/world) – permitted only if objectively true and not misleading
Secret / Confidentiel (secret/confidential) – prohibited due to potential for misleading public trust
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_reservation_validity_window_note: France does not maintain a formal 'name reservation' procedure comparable to common-law jurisdictions. This 30-day de facto window represents the validity of a name prior to adverse opposition, reflecting the typical period during which a pre-incorporation search report and trademark search may be relied upon. The actual name is only protected upon completion of the RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry (INPI/RNE) or the court-competent registrar issues a name rejection, the applicant receives an official refusal within 15 working days via the guichet unique. The applicant may (1) file a new proposed name through the same guichet unique portal without additional fee; (2) if the rejection is based on prior trademark rights, file a response or opposition brief with INPI under the IP Code; (3) appeal an administrative or registry decision before the competent Tribunal Judiciaire (technical rejection) or Tribunal de Commerce within 15 calendar days of notification, attaching the full dossier and a supporting legal argument; (4) request an administrative reconsideration from the INPI/RNE for an additional 30-day review period. The appeal should be lodged by a French-qualified lawyer or avocat.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_substance_requirements: Under Article L. 210-6 of the French Commercial Code, an SAS must have a registered office (siège social) in France or the European Economic Area with a physical address for legal service. A functional production facility is required for the activity stated under ISIC 2790 (manufacture of grid-tie solar inverters), and the registered office should be the principal production site or an administrative office where records, powers, and directors' appointments are kept in accordance with Article L. 232-21 (annual filings).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office / business domiciliation is permissible only via a licensed third-party 'domiciliataire' (e.g., Regus, Startway, etc.) under Law 2002-387 and Decree 2006-225. However, for a manufacturing entity under ISIC 2790, a virtual office alone cannot satisfy the 'commercial substance' or 'economic presence' test. The French tax administration and TRACFIN will treat a virtual office as a mere accommodation if no production operations, local staff, or operating assets are located in France. For VAT and corporate income tax purposes, a permanent establishment (PE) risk of 80% arises if only a virtual office is used.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For an industrial manufacturer with an operational production facility, the quantified risk of an unannounced on-site physical inspection by tax authorities (Direction générale des finances publiques), Urssaf, or the Ministry of Economy within the first 18 months is low at 5-10%. If a virtual office is used without a physical facility, the likelihood rises to 70-80% within 12 months, as required under the anti-abuse doctrine and the Duty of Vigilance (loi sur le devoir de vigilance).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory company name and legal form availability search (INPI/Infogreffe database)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) / Infogreffe (private legal registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official tariff (≈€35) plus market data report (≈€10)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized execution of Articles of Association (Statuts) for SAS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff under Decree 78-262 (rémunération des notaires) – fixed or quota-litteram fee; market benchmark €250-500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and conflict check for proposed corporate name and trademark (including UBO verification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: hourly rate €250-400/hour; flat-fee engagement for UBO piercing and name clearance ≈ €800-1,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of foreign corporate documents (e.g., Parent company Kbis equivalent, certificate of good standing, passport copies, powers of attorney) – per document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (France) or competent authority of the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular/Apostille official tariff (typically €25-40 per document); agency handling fee if used

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office or business domiciliation service for the first year (licensed domiciliataire)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation company (e.g., Regus, Independent brokers)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: €50-80/month for commercial registered office, first year minimum €600

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation filing fee via Guichet Unique (RCS registration fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee per Appendix of Decree No. 2019-969; cost ≈ €35-55 depending on entity type and online filing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, including Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9, L.227-1 to L.227-20, L.123-1 et seq., and applicable provisions on beneficial ownership declarations. The SAS is also subject to the Civil Code provisions governing contracts and legal personality.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés maintained by the competent commercial court clerk.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company formation through the INPI Guichet unique, supported by the signed SAS articles of association, capital deposit certificate, legal notice publication certificate, and beneficial ownership declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS; capital may legally be set at EUR 1. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash capital must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, which issues the deposit certificate. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed at incorporation and may require a commissaire aux apports report, subject to statutory exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President records that the Company has been duly incorporated as a Société par Actions Simplifiée under French law. The Company accepts the subscription of the shares described in the articles of association and confirms receipt of the required paid-up cash capital into the designated deposit account. The registered office is adopted at [full French address]. [Name] is appointed President for the term and under the powers specified in the articles. [Name], if applicable, is appointed Directeur Général. The officers are authorized to complete registration, tax, banking, beneficial ownership, employment, licensing, and regulatory formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Structure and Prepare SAS Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique for formalities; competent commercial court clerk for RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the corporate name, registered office, duration, share capital, share classes, governance rules, corporate purpose, President, and any Directeur Général. Draft and sign the articles in French. Verify that the corporate purpose covers manufacture, assembly, import, export, distribution, installation support, maintenance, and related solar power electronics activities.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and officers
Proof of address for each individual officer
Corporate extracts and authority documents for corporate shareholders
Registered-office title, lease, domiciliation agreement, or host certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent names, addresses, corporate purpose wording, powers of attorney, or identification data and resubmit through the INPI portal. Obtain a revised domiciliation or host certificate where the registered office evidence is rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal habilité à publier des annonces légales in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory incorporation notice to an authorized legal-notices publication service. Ensure that the notice identifies the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose summary, duration, President, and registration authority. Obtain the signed attestation of publication for the INPI filing.
required_dossiers: Final signed articles or validated incorporation data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice or republication if mandatory particulars are missing or inconsistent with the articles. Upload the corrected attestation and ensure the filing data exactly matches the published notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital and Obtain Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account in the company's formation name. Transfer the subscribed cash capital, provide beneficial ownership and source-of-funds information, and obtain the certificate of deposit. Do not release or use the funds until the company receives its registration evidence and the bank converts or opens the operating account.
required_dossiers: Shareholder identity and corporate authority documents
Draft legal-notice publication or publication attestation
Bank account opening and mandate forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to enhanced due diligence requests with certified corporate documents, ownership charts, tax-residence information, and source-of-funds evidence. If the bank declines onboarding, obtain a written refusal and apply to another authorized depositary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the creation form electronically, select SAS and the relevant commercial and manufacturing activities, upload the signed articles, capital certificate, publication attestation, registered-office proof, officer declarations, and beneficial ownership filing. Use qualified electronic identification or the prescribed filing authentication and pay the applicable registry and beneficial ownership charges.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI filing dashboard and answer the clerk's query within the stated deadline. Upload replacement documents in the requested format, pay any additional charge, and correct the formalities rather than filing a duplicate application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Registration Evidence and Activate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court clerk and INPI Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN, SIRET, APE classification, and Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence. Convert the capital account into an operating account, maintain the statutory registers, issue share ownership records, record the first board or shareholder resolutions, and implement accounting, tax, payroll, insurance, and data-protection controls.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract or RCS registration evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of an erroneous SIRET, APE code, officer identity, or registered-office entry through the INPI correction procedure and, where required, directly with the commercial court clerk or relevant public authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Industrial Site and Product Compliance Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant prefecture, DREAL regional environmental directorate, local mairie, SDIS departmental fire and rescue service, and labour and occupational-health authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing manufacturing, classify the site under the ICPE nomenclature, including storage, batteries, solvents, coating, waste, testing, and combustion equipment. File an ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization where thresholds apply. Obtain building, fire, workplace, and environmental approvals and implement CE, EMC, low-voltage, RoHS, WEEE, and applicable grid-connection product compliance for the inverters.
required_dossiers: Noise, emissions, wastewater, and waste-management assessments
Occupational risk assessment and prevention plan
CE technical file and declarations of conformity
ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization dossier, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to DREAL, prefectural, mairie, SDIS, or labour-authority observations with revised plans and technical evidence. Suspend the affected activity until the required declaration, registration, authorization, or corrective inspection is completed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The relevant prefecture, supported by the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL). France generally has no universal manufacturing licence for solar inverters; environmental and site permits are conditional on the installation's ICPE classification and local construction rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) declaration, registration, or authorization, as applicable under the French Environmental Code; supplemented by building, occupancy, fire-safety, and local planning approvals.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, with environmental assessment review by the competent regional environmental authority, typically the Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale (MRAe), and permitting administration through the prefecture and DREAL.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening. Ordinary inverter assembly may be exempt from a full EIA if no applicable Environmental Code threshold is met. Activities involving significant chemical use, coating, combustion, hazardous-material storage, waste treatment, or other listed ICPE thresholds may require a case-by-case environmental assessment, registration dossier, or full EIA and authorization.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single inverter-specific national limit applies. The operator must comply with the applicable ICPE prescriptions and prefectural order for wastewater, hazardous substances, VOCs, noise, air emissions, storage, and waste. Discharges must not pollute soil or water; hazardous waste must be separately identified, stored, tracked, and transferred to authorized operators through required waste-tracking documentation. Applicable occupational exposure limits and product-substance restrictions, including REACH and RoHS, must also be observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening the site, verify building conformity, fire compartments, escape routes, alarm and suppression systems, emergency access, hazardous-material storage, and electrical safety with the mairie, SDIS, and applicable building-control professionals. Structural load and industrial-equipment inspections must be documented. The employer must complete the DUERP occupational-risk assessment, provide workplace training and personal protective equipment, arrange occupational-health monitoring, and comply with Labour Code requirements. Public-access areas may require ERP safety and accessibility authorization.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — operating under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; official portal: impots.gouv.fr; online corporate and VAT registration platform: Guichet Unique administered by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); customs and export control authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), portal douane.gouv.fr (DELTA-X and CDE systems).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SAS through the INPI Guichet Unique, filing the statuts, the beneficial-owner declaration (RBE) and the appointment of the président; a minimum capital is not legally required for the SAS (optionally fixed in the statuts or by a capital increase). Step 2 — The Guichet Unique transmits the registration to the INSEE (SIRENE) and to the DGFiP; the entity receives the SIREN/SIRET identifiers and is automatically enrolled for corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés) with its local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). Step 3 — Upon issuance of the RCS extract (greffe du tribunal de commerce), the SAS applies for its French intra-community VAT number (format FR + 13 digits) with the SIE; the number is activated and validated through the EU VIES exchange system. Step 4 — For a foreign entity that does not incorporate a French subsidiary but has a taxable French permanent establishment, a direct Form No. 3707-SD (Cerfa 12373) application must be lodged with the local SIE before the first taxable transaction, and the appointment of an accredited VAT fiscal representative may be required for non-EU principals under article 289-A of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI). Step 5 — The completed tax identity package must include the RCS certificate, the VAT number confirmation letter, the SIRET data record, and confirmation of the registered office and bank account details to be used on all future invoices and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SAS is statutorily opaque and subject to corporate income tax at entity level under article 206 CGI; there is no check-the-box or partnership-taxation regime for an SAS. Available statutory elections include: (i) tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under articles 223 A to 223 U CGI where the parent holds at least 95% of the SAS capital; (ii) formation of a French VAT group (assujetti unique) under article 1693 ter CGI for closely related established taxable persons; (iii) election of the reduced 15% IS rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for PME enterprises under article 219 CGI, with the balance taxed at 25%; (iv) option for the EU One-Stop Shop (OSS) non-Union and Union schemes under articles 293 A to 293 F CGI for distance sales of solar inverters to final consumers within the European Union; (v) anti-hybrid and interest limitation elections and documentation safe harbours under articles 212 bis and 223 quinquies B CGI; and (vi) the option under article 262 ter CGI to zero-rate intra-EU supplies of inverters only upon receiving and verifying the customer's valid intra-community VAT number and lodging the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) — French value added tax governed by articles 256 to 289-H of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI) and Annexe II and III, transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC as amended by Directive (EU) 2021/2101, administered by the DGFiP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — a French SAS carrying on the manufacture of solar inverters is subject to compulsory VAT registration from its first taxable supply, with no turnover threshold; by way of parallel benchmark, the franchise en base de TVA (small-business exemption) under article 293 B CGI exempts enterprises with annual turnover below EUR 85,000 (sales of goods) or EUR 37,500 (services) in the prior calendar year, but this exemption is not practically available for a manufacturer realizing intra-EU acquisitions, export refunds or B2B invoicing to EU customers; for a non-established foreign seller making distance sales to French consumers, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 distance-selling registration threshold applies under the OSS regime (article 293 A CGI), below which VAT remains chargeable in the seller's home member state and above which French VAT becomes due.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has enacted the mandatory e-invoicing/e-reporting reform (Loi de finances pour 2020, implementing decrees and BOI-TVA-DECL-30-10-30) based on a Y-model with no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping as in Latin American jurisdictions. B2B invoices must be issued in a structured data format (Factur-X, UBL or CII national subset) and transmitted electronically through either a certified Partenaire de Dématérialisation (PDP) or the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); e-reporting of transaction data (B2C and cross-border flows) to the DGFiP is separate. Phased entry into force: from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and ETI (midcaps), and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro enterprises, including French taxable persons with annual turnover below the SME thresholds; mandated API interoperability requires the ERP invoicing module to generate the structured invoice, transmit the payload to the chosen PDP and synchronise the e-reporting datasets, while invoices intended for export zero-rating must retain the customs declaration references (MRN) and the export proof documents within the digital archiving chain; import and export clearances of inverters are processed through the DELTA/DEB and CDE/DES interfaces of the DGDDI, and there is no tax stamping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A French SAS exporting grid-tie solar inverters and microinverters may apply the 0% VAT rate (exonération avec droit à déduction) under article 262 (I) CGI for goods physically transported outside the customs territory of the European Union, provided the exporter holds contemporaneous documentary evidence that the goods left the EU within 90 days of the supply (administratively accepted up to 12 months by DGFiP doctrine BOI-TVA-CHAMP-30-20-20-10); intra-EU supplies of inverters to a customer established in another member state are zero-rated under article 262 ter CGI only where the customer's VAT identification number is valid and confirmed through VIES at the time of invoicing, the goods are dispatched to the other member state, and the supply is reported in the EC Sales List (récapitulatif des livraisons) and in the VAT return; installation, commissioning and offshore monitoring services delivered outside the EU qualify for exemption under articles 259-A, 259-B and 262 (II) CGI; each exempted invoice must state the legal basis ('TVA non applicable — art. 262-I or art. 262 ter CGI'), the exporter's French VAT number and, for intra-EU operations, the customer's VAT number.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique — DAU) lodged through the DELTA-X system and assigned a Movement Reference Number (MRN), including the exporter identification, the solar inverter tariff classification (HS 8504.40 for static converters), the customs value and the export procedure, together with the DELTA exit report confirming the goods' departure from the EU customs territory

Commercial Invoice issued by the French SAS matching the customs declaration value, the terms of delivery (Incoterms 2020), the inverter serial numbers, the applicable 0% VAT mention and the customer statutory data

Bill of Lading (sea freight), CMR consignment note (road haulage), Air Waybill (air freight) or an electronic transport record evidencing the physical removal of the goods from the EU to the destination customs office

Certificate of Origin (preferential EUR.1 / EUR-MED movement certificate, or a statement on origin under the REX registration system) where the buyer claims a preferential tariff conclusion under an EU free trade agreement, optionally supported by the exporter's Approved Exporter authorisation

Inward Remittance Certificate (justificatif de rapatriement de recettes d'exportation) — a bank confirmation from a French or EU credit institution evidencing that the EUR sales proceeds from the foreign customer were credited to the exporter's account, including the SWIFT reference, the amount and the corresponding invoice number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Legal exposure for fraudulent or abusive zero-rating includes: (i) immediate reassessment of the VAT unduly exempted, plus intérêts de retard computed under article 1727 CGI at the rate of 0.20% per month or per commenced period of 30 days, and an additional majoration of 40% for bad faith under article 1729 CGI or 80% for manoeuvres frauduleuses under article 1729-1 CGI; (ii) where the exemption claim is based on invoices or export evidence knowingly or negligently inaccurate, the amende fiscale of 50% of the sums involved under article 1788 A CGI applies separately; (iii) if the exporter failed to verify the validity of the customer's intra-Community VAT number before zero-rating an EU cross-border supply, the supplier becomes liable for the VAT under articles 283-1 and 262 ter CGI, with no subsequent deduction if the customer subsequently disappears (fraude carrousel); (iv) customs criminal penalties under the French code des douanes articles 414 and 415 apply to false export declarations and monetary fraud, ranging from fines of 1 to 3 times the value of the goods (up to 7 times where the fraud affects a right of export) and imprisonment of up to 5 years, extended to 10 years for organised fraud; (v) the DGFiP may claw back wrongly applied exemptions within the statute of limitation comprising 6 years generally under article L. 181 du Livre des procédures fiscales, extended to 10 years where the taxable activity was concealed or carried on by the exporter without filing VAT returns, with the burden of proof of the export remaining with the exporter throughout the retention period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France's national central bank and part of the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank sets euro-area monetary policy. The Direction générale du Trésor administers France's foreign-investment screening regime; it is not the foreign-exchange regulator.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France has no general foreign-exchange controls or distinction imposing routine exchange restrictions between current-account and capital-account transactions. The euro is freely convertible, and a French SAS may generally receive, hold, convert, and remit funds domestically or cross-border, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing rules, tax requirements, bank controls, and applicable EU or French investment-screening rules. Dividends and other profit distributions may be paid abroad after corporate-law authorization, availability of distributable profits, withholding-tax analysis, and any applicable treaty or EU-law conditions. Interest, royalties, service fees, and loan repayments require genuine underlying transactions, appropriate documentation, transfer-pricing support where relevant, and tax withholding analysis. Banks may require evidence of source of funds, beneficial ownership, business purpose, and tax status. France does not generally require prior central-bank approval for ordinary commercial payments or capital transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds to France by a specified deadline or to convert a prescribed percentage into euros. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign currency or in an overseas account, subject to tax, accounting, sanctions, contractual, and bank-reporting requirements. Banks may request invoices, customs or transport documentation, and payment-purpose information. Separate statistical reporting obligations may apply to certain cross-border transactions or entities under Banque de France rules; applicability and thresholds should be checked for the entity and reporting period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account before registration, if required by the formation process and accepted by the bank; operational business account after incorporation
Capital deposit account before registration, if required by the formation process and accepted by the bank; operational business account after incorporation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant regional Crédit Agricole caisse
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account before registration, if required by the formation process and accepted by the bank; operational business account after incorporation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. and the relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne institution
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account before registration, if required by the formation process and accepted by the bank; operational business account after incorporation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for routine payments and foreign-currency collections; low as the sole banking arrangement during incorporation or for complex trade finance. An electronic money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts and cross-border transfers if duly authorized in France or passported into France under EU rules. Electronic-money balances are safeguarded under applicable rules but are not bank deposits covered by the French deposit-guarantee scheme. Confirm the provider's authorization, safeguarding arrangements, permitted services, account ownership, currencies, transfer limits, and support for SWIFT, letters of credit, guarantees, and tax or capital-deposit requirements. Offshore status alone does not establish authorization to serve French customers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal in-person bank-account opening or director-interview requirement for a SAS. Remote onboarding may be available, subject to the bank's risk policy, identity-verification standards, and ability to verify the company, representatives, beneficial owners, and source of funds. A bank may require an in-person meeting, certified or legalized documents, French-language materials, or a French address. Capital-deposit procedures and pre-incorporation accounts are bank-specific; confirm the required sequence and documents directly with the selected institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or layered ownership, opaque trusts, nominee shareholders, or inability to identify natural-person beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry extracts and constitutional documents for each ownership-chain entity; certified ownership chart to natural persons; beneficial-owner register filing information where applicable; identity and address evidence for beneficial owners and directors; trust or nominee documents where relevant; explanations for control rights; and proof of source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unusual capital contribution, third-party funding, unexplained shareholder loan, or payment from a jurisdiction inconsistent with the business profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription and shareholder-loan agreements; board or shareholder resolutions; bank statements evidencing the remitting party and funds trail; audited accounts, sale documents, dividend records, or other source-of-funds evidence; remitter relationship explanation; and a transaction-specific payment narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Solar inverter products, counterparties, destinations, or technical specifications raise sanctions, export-control, or dual-use concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product catalogue and technical specifications; classification analysis under applicable EU export-control rules; end-user and end-use statements; customer and beneficial-owner screening records; destination and route details; export licences or documented basis for non-licensing; and written sanctions-screening procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value or repetitive international receipts and payments with weak linkage to genuine trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed contracts and purchase orders; commercial invoices; shipping, customs, and delivery records; supplier and customer due-diligence files; reconciliation of expected payment flows to projected turnover; and a documented explanation of intermediaries, payment-on-behalf arrangements, or deviations from contractual terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear French operating substance, newly formed entity, or mismatch between declared business activity and payment flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract or other current registration evidence; statutes; registered-office and premises evidence; business plan and financial forecast; director and employee information; supplier and customer pipeline; tax registration details; and explanation of manufacturing, distribution, and inventory arrangements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscriptions and shareholder funding from an account held in the investor's or lender's own name, preferably through an EU/EEA bank or a regulated bank with a clear correspondent-banking trail. Use the bank's designated capital-deposit process where funds are paid before incorporation; obtain the deposit certificate required for registration and transfer the funds to the operational account after incorporation in accordance with bank instructions. For post-incorporation equity, provide the subscription documentation and corporate approvals. For shareholder loans, use a written loan agreement, corporate authorization, documented commercial terms, and transfer-pricing review where applicable. Include accurate payer, beneficiary, currency, and transaction-purpose information in the SWIFT payment message and retain contracts, resolutions, and source-of-funds evidence. There is no universal French foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary commercial wires; comply with the sending and receiving banks' message-field requirements and any applicable statistical reporting requests. Screen parties, banks, and jurisdictions against applicable sanctions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the scheme's geographic and service scope. Use SWIFT customer credit transfers, commonly MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments; provide complete beneficiary, bank, invoice, contract, and payment-purpose details. For large equipment or component purchases, documentary letters of credit, including commercial documentary credits subject to agreed UCP 600 terms, may be used through a bank willing to issue or advise them; align credit terms with shipping, inspection, and document requirements. Alternatives include documentary collections, bank guarantees, and advance or open-account settlement after counterparty and credit-risk review. Reconcile payments to purchase orders, invoices, customs documentation, and delivery evidence; apply sanctions and export-control screening before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for documented commercial exposures, subject to the bank's suitability, credit, and documentation requirements
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency conversion management, subject to counterparty limits and contract documentation
Currency options or structured foreign-exchange products where appropriate, after suitability and product-risk review

Non-deliverable forwards only where the currency, counterparty, and transaction structure lawfully require or support cash settlement; they are not a substitute for deliverable hedging where delivery is feasible

Derivatives entered into or marketed in the EU remain subject to applicable MiFID II conduct and product-governance requirements, EMIR reporting, clearing, margin, and risk-mitigation rules as applicable to the entity and transaction; determine the SAS's counterparty classification and hedging exemption status before execution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval by the sole shareholder or shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing authority; approval is recorded in the company's corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A court may order the legal representative to convene the shareholders and may impose a daily coercive fine; no automatic strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the Registry of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Clerk of the competent Commercial Court, through the RCS filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in a court injunction and a civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, increasing to EUR 3,000 for a repeat offense. No automatic strike-off deadline applies; prolonged inactivity may lead to administrative deregistration after notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year accounting period, by the second working day after 1 May, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased in specified circumstances, plus late-payment interest; no corporate strike-off is triggered solely by a late tax return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information update, if reportable information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Clerk of the competent Commercial Court maintaining the National Register of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the company becomes aware of a change requiring an update; no annual confirmation is required if information remains unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate, complete, or timely information may result in criminal penalties for the company and its legal representative; no automatic strike-off timeline applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor if it exceeds at least two of these thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Lower thresholds apply to certain companies controlled by or controlling another company: EUR 2.5 million balance sheet, EUR 5 million net turnover, and 25 average employees. Appointment may also be required by law in specified group structures or by a court.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Accounting Standards (Plan comptable général) apply to individual statutory accounts. IFRS is required for consolidated accounts of entities whose securities are admitted to trading on an EU regulated market; other groups may be subject to applicable French consolidation rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no annual UBO confirmation filing solely because a year has elapsed. The SAS must file an update within 30 days after a change in reportable beneficial ownership or related particulars. Maintain current ownership records and supporting evidence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and share transfers, maintained in the company's records
Register of Directors and officers, maintained in the company's records
Minute Book containing shareholder and corporate decision records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,200 per year, depending on location and services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 4,000-15,000 per year for a small SAS; fees depend on complexity, group structure, and transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022). Reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with turnover below EUR 10 million and fully paid-up capital held 75% by individuals or qualifying entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Targeted incentives include: (i) Research Tax Credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche, CIR) equal to 30% of eligible R&D expenditures up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; (ii) Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs at 20% of eligible innovation expenditures up to EUR 400,000; (iii) accelerated depreciation for certain energy-efficiency and renewable-energy equipment; (iv) reduced 15% rate for qualifying SMEs; (v) exemption regime for young innovative companies (JEI) subject to conditions; (vi) territorial economic contribution (CET) comprising CFE and CVAE, with CVAE being phased out by 2027.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration annuelle de résultat (DSF) via the EDI-TVA / IS portal (impots.gouv.fr), using the fiscal year result schedule (liasse fiscale) including forms 2065 (IS), 2033-A to 2033-G or 2050-2059 for the simplified/regular regime, and mandatory e-filing for entities subject to IS.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly advance installment payments, acomptes provisionnels, and potential annual balance payment).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally within three months following the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, filing deadline is the second working day following 30 April of the following year (typically early May). Payment of the balance of IS is due by 15 May for calendar-year taxpayers. Advance installments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification including SIREN, company name, legal form (SAS), fiscal year start and end, and principal activity code (APE/NAF).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with a French permanent establishment or filing obligation must indicate the French tax identification number (if registered) or the foreign registration number and the address of the PE or representative in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065 Box B / Option for group taxation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indication of whether the entity files as part of a tax consolidation group (intégration fiscale) under Articles 223 A et seq. CGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent may only consolidate French subsidiaries if the parent is itself subject to French corporate tax on the relevant profits or if the consolidated group is formed under the conditions of Article 223 A CGI with a French subsidiary as head.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065 Line WA / Turnover and income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of total turnover (chiffre d'affaires) and net taxable income before offset of losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must report only income attributable to a French PE or French-source income subject to IS. Foreign-source income of the PE must be reported and a foreign tax credit may apply under applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065 Line WR / Tax due after credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net corporate income tax due after application of tax credits, including CIR/CII, foreign tax credits and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents should attach supporting documentation for treaty-based credits and ensure advance payments made in France are deducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable profit, including disallowed expenses, non-deductible depreciation, provisions, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must include adjustments for transactions with related parties and explain any items treated differently under French tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of capital gains and losses, including long-term capital gains regime and exemption for qualifying share disposals under the participation-exemption regime (régime des sociétés mères et filiales, Article 145 CGI).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may benefit from the participation-exemption regime if the conditions (5% holding, two-year holding period, French or EU/EEA parent satisfying Article 145) are met; otherwise, gains attributable to French PE are taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed reporting of tax credits, including CIR, CII, and foreign tax credits under DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents should attach the DTA article, foreign tax certificate, and TRC if relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065 Box C / Signature and certification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature by a legal representative or authorized agent, with certification of accuracy.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities may authorize a French tax representative (mandataire) or use the accredited e-filing procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge for delay not exceeding 30 days; 20% for delay between 30 days and 90 days; 40% for delay exceeding 90 days or upon formal notice (mise en demeure); 80% in cases of concealed activity or aggravated circumstances. Late payment interest: 0.20% per month of delay (2.4% annual) plus a 5% surcharge for failure to pay within the statutory deadline. Additional 10% penalty for insufficient advance payments. Non-compliance with e-filing obligations may trigger a EUR 15 penalty per document or 0.2% of the declared amounts, subject to caps.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% standard withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-residents (Article 119 bis CGI). However, a reduced rate of 12.8% applies to dividends paid to individuals resident in France; for non-residents, the 30% withholding applies unless reduced by an applicable DTA. Note: The French domestic rate for non-resident dividends is 30% (prélèvement forfaitaire obligatoire for individuals, but for legal persons the standard withholding is 30% unless treaty relief). EU parent-subsidiary directive may exempt dividends to qualifying EU parent companies (25% holding, two years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (i) Non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority; (ii) Provide Form 5000 (formerly 5000-SD) or equivalent simplified certificate for individuals/entities, and Form 5009 for certain entities, to the paying agent/withholding agent before payment, or within the applicable deadline; (iii) The French withholding agent applies the reduced treaty rate at source or the non-resident may claim a refund of the excess withholding by filing Form 5002 within two years from the end of the year of payment (for individuals) or by the 31 December of the second year following the year of payment (for legal persons); (iv) For EU parent-subsidiary directive, provide evidence of 25% holding and two-year holding period. Additional anti-abuse provisions (Article 119 bis 2 and Article 187 CGI) may deny relief if the arrangement is considered abusive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding tax rate 33.33% (reduced to 30% for payments to non-cooperative states; 75% for payments to non-cooperative states). Treaty rates typically 0-10% under French DTAs. Interest: statutory withholding tax rate 33.33% (30% for certain payments; 75% to non-cooperative states). Treaty rates typically 0-15%. EU Interest and Royalties Directive may exempt qualifying payments between associated EU companies (25% direct holding, two years). Domestic exemption for interest paid to EU/EEA parents under certain conditions. Payments to non-resident entities in non-cooperative states subject to 75% withholding regardless of treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File required for French entities that are part of a group with consolidated turnover exceeding EUR 50 million and that are subject to TP documentation requirements (Article 223 quinquies B CGI). Local File required for French entities with annual turnover or gross balance sheet exceeding EUR 400 million, or belonging to a group with such thresholds, and for entities with transactions with related parties exceeding EUR 100,000 per transaction or EUR 1 million aggregate per year (thresholds may vary; the statutory threshold for mandatory TP documentation is EUR 400 million turnover for the Local File, and the Master File threshold is EUR 50 million). However, the French Tax Code requires TP documentation for entities that are dependent or controlling and that have related-party transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 per transaction or EUR 1 million aggregate. In practice, the documentation obligation is triggered at EUR 400 million turnover for the full Local File, but the tax authority may request TP documentation for smaller entities on audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies a general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit, Article L64 LPF) and specific anti-abuse provisions. Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as such do not exist; however, substance is assessed under the abus de droit doctrine and the concept of 'acte anormal de gestion' (abnormal management act). For foreign entities, France may apply Article 209 B CGI (controlled foreign company rules) if the entity is subject to a privileged tax regime and predominantly passive income. French TP rules require that intercompany transactions comply with the arm's length principle under Article 57 CGI. For SAS entities, no specific statutory economic substance requirement, but the tax authority examines actual decision-making, risk control, and functions performed. The EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) has been transposed, including interest limitation rules, CFC rules, and exit taxation. Beneficial ownership and PPT (Principal Purpose Test) apply under DTAs following MLI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of taxable income, fraudulent filing, or deliberate understatement of tax due, including use of fictitious invoices or false documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 40% or 80% of unpaid tax; criminal penalty of EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment for tax fraud (Article 1741 CGI). Aggravated fraud (e.g., use of offshore accounts) may result in EUR 2,000,000 fine and 7 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives (président, directeurs) may be held personally liable for civil restitution of tax debts in case of fraud or mismanagement (Article 1745 CGI; action en comblement de passif). Criminal conviction may include imprisonment and a ban on managing companies (faillite personnelle). Travel bans may be imposed for unpaid tax debts exceeding EUR 50,000 under certain conditions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to provide TP documentation upon request, or failure to demonstrate arm's length pricing, or unilaterally adjusting profits without corresponding adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of EUR 10,000 per year for failure to provide documentation; increased to EUR 50,000 in case of repeat offense. Additional reassessment of taxable income and 40% penalty for insufficient documentation if the taxpayer fails to justify pricing. Under Article 57 CGI, the tax authority may adjust taxable income to arm's length, with penalties of 40% or 80% for intentional mispricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they participated in the non-compliant pricing or failed to implement compliance procedures. Criminal liability for tax fraud may apply if the mispricing is intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform customer due diligence, failure to report suspicious transactions, or failure to maintain adequate records, particularly for cross-border wire transfers and LC transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of turnover for serious breaches; criminal penalties of up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine for money laundering (Article 324-1 Code pénal). The ACPR may impose sanctions including withdrawal of license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for fines and imprisonment for AML violations. They may also face professional bans and disgorgement of profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing an entity with no economic substance solely for tax avoidance, treaty shopping, or circumvention of French tax obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of treaty benefits, reassessment of profits, and penalties of 80% for abuse of law (abus de droit). The entity may be requalified as a French tax resident or its income reallocated. Penalties under Article 1729 CGI (80%) and Article 1759 (aggravated).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for tax debts and penalties, and may face criminal prosecution for tax fraud and money laundering. Travel bans and asset freezes may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Late filing or non-filing of annual corporate income tax returns despite obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharges of 10%, 20%, 40%, or 80% depending on delay and whether a formal notice has been issued. Late payment interest of 0.20% per month. In case of concealed activity, 80% penalty and additional criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the tax and penalties if the failure is due to their fault, especially in case of liquidation or insolvency. They may also face criminal penalties for fraudulent non-filing.
